2026-09-23T03:55:32.7332110Z # Seven ctest registrations import numpy, Pillow or scikit-image and
2026-09-23T03:55:32.7332350Z # skip themselves when one of those is missing. A ctest SKIP reads
2026-09-23T03:55:32.7332590Z # exactly like a PASS, so a lane that quietly lost a wheel reports
2026-09-23T03:55:32.7332820Z # green without running the checks it was built for. Installing the
2026-09-23T03:55:32.7333030Z # declared set on every platform that runs ctest keeps the
2026-09-23T03:55:32.7333240Z # non-skippable visual-python-deps-present check answerable
2026-09-23T03:55:32.7333460Z # everywhere, rather than red on the platforms the install misses.
2026-09-23T03:55:32.7333620Z #
2026-09-23T03:55:32.7333760Z # The interpreter must be the one CMake configured, not whatever this
2026-09-23T03:55:32.7334020Z # shell resolves: ctest invokes Python3_EXECUTABLE, so installing into
2026-09-23T03:55:32.7334240Z # a different interpreter would leave every one of those tests
2026-09-23T03:55:32.7334440Z # skipping while this step reported success.
2026-09-23T03:55:32.7334570Z #
2026-09-23T03:55:32.7334720Z # find_package(Python3 COMPONENTS Interpreter) records the interpreter
2026-09-23T03:55:32.7334940Z # it resolved in the INTERNAL cache entry _Python3_EXECUTABLE and
2026-09-23T03:55:32.7335160Z # leaves the public Python3_EXECUTABLE a normal variable, so the
2026-09-23T03:55:32.7335370Z # public name reaches the cache only when a configure passes
2026-09-23T03:55:32.7335580Z # -DPython3_EXECUTABLE. The local Shipyard lane passes it; this
2026-09-23T03:55:32.7335850Z # workflow does not. Read the internal entry first — it holds the
2026-09-23T03:55:32.7336070Z # value the public variable expanded to when test/cmake registered
2026-09-23T03:55:32.7336290Z # these tests, which is exactly what ctest launches — and fall back to
2026-09-23T03:55:32.7336510Z # the public entry for a configure that pinned one explicitly.
2026-09-23T03:55:32.7336690Z cache="$PULP_BUILD_DIR/CMakeCache.txt"
2026-09-23T03:55:32.7336880Z py="$(sed -n 's/^_Python3_EXECUTABLE:[^=]*=//p' "$cache" | head -1)"
2026-09-23T03:55:32.7337050Z if [ -z "$py" ]; then
2026-09-23T03:55:32.7337210Z   py="$(sed -n 's/^Python3_EXECUTABLE:[^=]*=//p' "$cache" | head -1)"
2026-09-23T03:55:32.7337360Z fi
2026-09-23T03:55:32.7337450Z if [ -z "$py" ]; then
2026-09-23T03:55:32.7337600Z   echo "No Python3 interpreter is recorded in $cache" >&2
2026-09-23T03:55:32.7337810Z   echo "(looked for _Python3_EXECUTABLE, then Python3_EXECUTABLE)." >&2
2026-09-23T03:55:32.7338070Z   echo "The visual-analysis tests resolve their interpreter from that cache entry," >&2
2026-09-23T03:55:32.7338350Z   echo "so installing into any other interpreter would leave them skipping." >&2
2026-09-23T03:55:32.7338540Z   exit 1
2026-09-23T03:55:32.7338620Z fi
2026-09-23T03:55:32.7338750Z echo "Installing the declared visual-analysis set into $py"
2026-09-23T03:55:32.7339200Z # PEP 668 hosts (Homebrew, Debian) refuse a plain --user install; the
2026-09-23T03:55:32.7339410Z # second form is the sanctioned override for those hosts.
2026-09-23T03:55:32.7339640Z "$py" -m pip install --user --upgrade -r tools/motion/visual/requirements.txt || \
2026-09-23T03:55:32.7339950Z   "$py" -m pip install --break-system-packages --user --upgrade -r tools/motion/visual/requirements.txt
